Meet Odyssey-3 a foundation world model from Odyssey that generates interactive environments from a prompt and predicts, in real time, how they change as you or an AI agent act in them. Odyssey says it’s their most powerful world model yet.

You now get:

 Environments generated from a prompt, with first-person and third-person navigation and independent camera movement
 A model that predicts how objects move and interact and how situations evolve, learned from video
 The same model adapted to real machines: robot arms, humanoids and a car

What’s new? [...] What’s new?

1. Physical accuracy: Odyssey-3 Pro posts 66.1 on Physics-IQ Verified’s video-to-video benchmark (best-of-8 sampling), which Odyssey says is the highest reported score, and 54.7 on image-to-video. The benchmark tests fluid dynamics, optics, solid mechanics, magnetism and thermodynamics. Odyssey also says the standard model improves the tradeoff between physical accuracy and generation cost, so you get more simulations from the same compute.
2. Real-time interaction: Odyssey-3 reacts to actions and events as they happen. A distilled few-step version makes that fast enough for real-time use.

Odyssey has unveiled Odyssey-3, a foundation world model designed to work across physical and virtual environments.  
  
The company has demonstrated the same pretrained backbone behind robot arms, humanoids, cars, drones and video-game agents. It can also generate environments where other AI agents can act, learn and train.   
  
One of the most striking demos is driving: Odyssey says a researcher adapted the model to Indian roads using 20 hours of driving data, with simulation-trained policies reportedly reaching about 77% of the distance between safety-driver interventions achieved by its real-data-trained system.

#genai#robotics

Questions this post answers

What is Odyssey 3 Pro and how is it different from a regular video generation model?

Odyssey 3 Pro is a world model that goes beyond generating video: it takes visual observations from the world, learns how physical systems behave, and maps that knowledge onto physical controls. This lets the same model control a robot, drive a car, play a video game, or pilot a drone, rather than just producing video output. daily.dev surfaces emerging world model releases like this for engineers tracking generative AI beyond video generation.

Does Odyssey-3 actually rank first on the Physics-IQ Verified benchmark? [...] Odyssey 3 Pro is reported to rank number one among video-to-video models on the Physics-IQ Verified benchmark for physical accuracy, according to Odyssey's own claim and an independent reading of the leaderboard. The model is only available as a research preview, so the ranking has not been independently confirmed beyond that reporting. Developers evaluating world model benchmarks can follow claims like this on daily.dev before trusting vendor leaderboards.
